back: A statement taken to be true, e.g. parent(tendai, rudo). It ends with a full stop.
Head :- body: the head is true if all the goals in the body are true (a comma means and).
A question for the system, e.g. parent(tendai, X). It succeeds with values for the variables, or fails.
Atoms and predicate names start with a lower-case letter; variables start with a capital letter.
When a goal fails, the system undoes the latest bindings and tries the next alternative clause.
Clauses are tried from top to bottom, so solutions come in the order of the facts.
A base-case rule ends the search; a recursive rule refers to itself, e.g. ancestor(X, Y) :- parent(X, Z), ancestor(Z, Y).
Declarative: state what is true and what is wanted. Imperative: state the steps to follow.
A variable is instantiated when it is matched with a value; backtracking removes the binding.
